title: Insertion: Two Pointer Writes and One Walk
quickIdea: Insertion itself is a fixed pair of pointer writes, so it is O(1); what costs time is reaching the position, which is a walk from head unless you already hold the node.
remember: At the head: new->next = head; head = new;. Two writes, O(1), and the order is not free: head = new first loses the whole list.
After a given node p: new->next = p->next; p->next = new;. O(1). Reversing the two lines makes the new node point at itself.
At the tail: you must walk to the last node, so O(n). Keeping a tail pointer makes the append O(1), but then the tail pointer must be maintained on every insert and delete.
At position i: the walk is O(i) and the relinking is O(1), so the operation is O(n).
Inserting n elements into an empty list that must stay sorted costs Theta(n^2) in the worst case: the i-th insertion walks up to i-1 nodes, and 0 + 1 + ... + (n-1) = n(n-1)/2.
Inserting n elements at the head is Theta(n) in total, because every insertion is O(1) and no walk is needed.

example.prompt: Insert 25 after the node holding 20 in the list 10 -> 20 -> 30 -> NULL.
example.work: Hold p at the node 20. Set new->next = p->next, so the new node points at 30. Then set p->next = new, so 20 points at the new node. For 4 elements the walk from head to 20 is 2 steps.
example.answer: 10 -> 20 -> 25 -> 30 -> NULL, in two pointer writes plus the walk to find 20.

gateAngle: GATE asks for the cost of a sequence of insertions, not one insertion. GATE CSE 2020 Q.16 gives n elements into a sorted list and expects Theta(n^2) because each placement is a fresh walk; the same reasoning makes the sorted-insert variant of any 'n operations on a list' question quadratic.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2020 Q.16. What is the worst case time complexity of inserting n elements into an empty linked list if the list must be maintained in sorted order?
variations.why: The worst case is input arriving already sorted, so every new element belongs at the end and each insertion scans the whole current list: 0 + 1 + 2 + ... + (n-1) = n(n-1)/2 comparisons, which is Theta(n^2).

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: The same n elements are inserted at the head of an empty list instead, with no order requirement. What is the total cost, and what is the resulting order?
variations.answer: Theta(n) total, and the list holds the input in reverse order.
variations.why: Each insertion is two pointer writes with no walk, so the total is n writes. The order reverses because every new node becomes the head, which is the same mechanism a stack uses.

trap.what: Saying 'insertion in a linked list is O(1)' with no qualifier.
trap.why: Only the relinking is O(1). The position has to be found first, and finding it is a walk, so the operation is O(1) only when you already hold the node you insert after.
trap.counterexample: Inserting at the end of a 1000-node singly linked list with only a head pointer walks 999 links before the two writes. The writes are constant; the operation is not.

check.question: How many node visits are made in total when 5 elements arrive in sorted order and are inserted into a sorted linked list?
check.explanation: The i-th insertion scans i-1 existing nodes, so the total is 0+1+2+3+4 = 10 = 5*4/2. That sum is the reason the cost is quadratic rather than linear.
